help.intro: A short text of about 150 words about a German habit that confuses every visitor: the Pfand. On most bottles and cans you pay 25 cents extra, and you get the money back when you return the bottle to a machine in the supermarket. The text explains how it works, since when, what the two kinds of Pfand are, and why you see people collecting bottles in parks. The facts are real and were checked. You need what you have just learnt: the imperative for du and Sie (Wirf nicht weg! Bringen Sie die Flasche zurück!), the accusative (die Flasche, den Bon, das Geld) and nicht / kein for negation. Read for the gist first, then take each question to one sentence of the text.
help.tips[0].title: Imperative: du and Sie
help.tips[0].text: du form: take the du present, drop -st and du: du wirfst → Wirf! du bringst → Bring! du gibst → Gib! du nimmst → Nimm! Separable verbs split: Bring die Flasche zurück! Wirf sie nicht weg! Sie form: verb first, then Sie: Bringen Sie die Flasche zurück! Werfen Sie sie nicht weg! Plural ihr: Bringt die Flaschen zurück! A friendly bitte softens it: Gib mir bitte den Bon.
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: Do not throw the bottle away! Bring it back and get the money.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Press the green button and take the receipt.
help.tips[0].check.why: Drop -st and du from du gibst: Gib! Verbs with e → i keep the i.
help.tips[1].title: nicht or kein?
help.tips[1].text: kein negates a noun with ein or no article: Das ist kein Müll. Ich habe keine Flasche. nicht negates everything else: a verb, an adjective, a place, a noun with der/die/das: Wirf die Flasche nicht weg. Das Pfand ist nicht teuer. Die Flasche ist nicht im Automaten.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: The bottle is not rubbish. It is money.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The machine does not take the bottle? Then the label is damaged.
help.tips[1].check.why: A noun with ein (der Bon, einen Bon) is negated with kein, here accusative masculine: keinen.
help.remember[0]: Imperative du: Wirf! Bring … zurück! Nimm! Gib!  Sie: Bringen Sie …!
help.remember[1]: kein + noun (kein Müll, keinen Bon); nicht for everything else (nicht weg, nicht teuer).
help.exam: Short practical texts with instructions in the imperative and multiple-choice questions are a typical reading task at this level.
help.hook: In Germany an empty bottle is worth 25 cents, and a machine gives you the money. Read how the Pfand works and why people collect bottles in the park.
passageTranslation:
You buy a bottle of water in Germany. It costs one euro. But at the checkout you pay one euro twenty-five. Why? The 25 cents are deposit. You get the money back when you bring the bottle back.

This is how it works: drink the water. Do not throw the bottle away! Bring it to a supermarket. There stands a deposit machine. Put the bottle into the machine. The machine reads the label and gives you a receipt. With the receipt you go to the checkout and get your money.

The deposit has existed since 2003. There are two kinds: single-use bottles of thin plastic and cans carry 25 cents deposit. Reusable bottles of glass or thick plastic carry only 8 or 15 cents. These bottles are washed and refilled up to fifty times.

That is why you often see people with big bags in parks. They collect bottles. Ten bottles are two euros fifty. Many people therefore put their empty bottles next to the bin, not in it. That is not rubbish. That is money.
questions[0].explanation: "Aber an der Kasse bezahlst du einen Euro fünfundzwanzig. Warum? Die 25 Cent sind Pfand."
questions[0].questionTranslation: The bottle of water costs one euro. What do you pay at the checkout?
questions[0].optionsTranslation[3]: two euros fifty with the deposit for the bottle
questions[1].explanation: du wirfst weg → Wirf … weg! The separable verb wegwerfen splits, and nicht stands before weg.
questions[1].questionTranslation: 'Do not throw the bottle away!' Which form is that?
questions[1].optionsTranslation[0]: imperative, du form, separable verb wegwerfen
questions[1].optionsTranslation[2]: imperative, Sie form, polite: Werfen Sie die Flasche nicht weg
questions[2].explanation: "Der Automat liest das Etikett und gibt dir einen Bon. Mit dem Bon gehst du zur Kasse und bekommst dein Geld."
questions[2].questionTranslation: What does the deposit machine do?
questions[2].optionsTranslation[1]: It gives you the water back.
questions[2].optionsTranslation[2]: It reads the label and gives you a receipt.
questions[2].optionsTranslation[3]: It gives you the money directly in your hand, without receipt and without checkout.
questions[3].questionTranslation: Since when has the deposit existed?
questions[4].explanation: "Einwegflaschen aus dünnem Plastik und Dosen haben 25 Cent Pfand."
questions[4].questionTranslation: How much deposit does a can carry?
questions[5].explanation: "Diese Flaschen werden gewaschen und bis zu fünfzig Mal neu gefüllt."
questions[5].optionsTranslation[1]: They are washed and refilled up to fifty times.
questions[5].optionsTranslation[2]: They carry 25 cents deposit and are thrown away afterwards.
questions[6].explanation: "Sie sammeln Flaschen. Zehn Flaschen sind zwei Euro fünfzig."
questions[6].questionTranslation: Why do you see people with big bags in parks?
questions[6].optionsTranslation[1]: They collect bottles for the deposit.
questions[6].optionsTranslation[2]: They take the rubbish out of the park and get money from the city for it.
questions[7].explanation: A noun without an article (Müll) is negated with kein; nicht would be used for verbs, adjectives or nouns with der/die/das.
questions[7].questionTranslation: 'That is not rubbish. That is money.' Why kein and not nicht?
questions[7].optionsTranslation[0]: because Müll is a noun without an article
questions[7].optionsTranslation[1]: because the sentence is a question and questions always need kein
questions[7].optionsTranslation[3]: because kein always stands at the end of the sentence
questions[1].options[2]: Imperativ, Sie-Form, höflich: Werfen Sie die Flasche nicht weg
questions[2].options[1]: Er gibt dir das Wasser zurück.
questions[2].options[2]: Er liest das Etikett und gibt dir einen Bon.
questions[2].options[3]: Er gibt dir direkt das Geld in die Hand, ohne Bon und ohne Kasse.
